title: Cook Pine: Ancient Cook Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Brisbane's Cook pine, planted by Prince Albert in 1868, is now the tallest tree in the City Botanic Gardens. Three mapped across three continents.
intro: Cook pine comes from one stretch of the Pacific, New Caledonia's Isle of Pines, where eighteenth-century sailors mistook its narrow, leaning columns for stone and named the island after the mistake. Planted as an ornamental far from home, it tends to end up the tallest thing around: Brisbane's, one of two set out by Prince Albert, Duke of Edinburgh, in 1868, is now the tallest tree in the City Botanic Gardens at forty-five metres. Lima's stands inside a seventeenth-century Spanish olive grove and has already outgrown trees three centuries older than it. Palermo's rises thirty-eight metres over Villa Tasca's swan lake, the pine on one shore answering a fig tree's shade on the other.
